## Ontario Lease Visit Snapshot
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/house.svg

This looks like a standard Ontario residential tenancy scenario, with one important caveat: in Ontario, a “security deposit” is generally not the usual legal term for rent deposits, so the exact deposit type matters. For the entry request, the practical issue is whether the landlord gave proper written notice and whether the repair visit is at a reasonable time.

## Tenant Rights and Landlord Duties Checklist
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/clipboard-check.svg

- **Lease status:** A 12-month lease starting **2025-09-01** would normally run to **2026-08-31**, so the tenancy is still in the fixed term on **2026-03-15**.
- **Entry notice:** In Ontario, a landlord usually needs **at least 24 hours’ written notice** to enter for repairs, with the **reason**, **date**, **time window**, and **entry window**.
- **Timing:** The visit should generally be during a **reasonable time of day**; the notice should identify when entry will happen.
- **Purpose:** Repairs are a valid reason to enter, but the landlord should limit entry to what is necessary for the work.
- **Deposit:** If the deposit was a lawful Ontario deposit type, it should be handled according to the Residential Tenancies Act rules; if it was called a “security deposit,” it may not match Ontario’s usual deposit structure.
- **Tenant response:** The tenant can politely ask for the notice details in writing, confirm access arrangements, and request the contractor/repair scope.
- **Practical recordkeeping:** Keep the lease, notice, texts/emails, and any photos of the unit condition before and after the repair.

## Practical Checklist for the Tenant
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/check2-square.svg

- Confirm the notice is **written** and includes the **repair reason**, **date**, **time**, and **approximate entry window**.
- Check that the notice was given **at least 24 hours before** the entry time.
- Reply politely confirming the landlord may enter **if the notice is complete**.
- Ask who is coming: **landlord, contractor, or repair company**.
- Ask whether anyone will need to enter **multiple times** or if it is a **one-time visit**.
- Secure valuables and note the unit’s condition before the visit.
- If the notice is incomplete, reply asking for a corrected notice rather than refusing outright.
- If the landlord changes the time, ask for an updated written notice.

## Polite Email to Confirm the Repair Visit
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/envelope.svg

Subject: Repair Visit on March 15, 2026

Hello [Landlord’s Name],

Thank you for the notice about the repair visit on March 15, 2026.

I’m writing to confirm that I understand the visit is for repairs. Please let me know the expected time window, who will be attending, and whether any additional access will be needed.

If the notice changes, please send the updated details in writing. I’ll make sure the unit is accessible at the scheduled time.

Thank you,
[Tenant’s Name]

## Sources
- Ontario Residential Tenancies Act overview: https://www.ontario.ca/laws/statute/06r17
- Landlord and Tenant Board – notices and entry rules: https://tribunalsontario.ca/ltb/
- Government of Ontario – renting in Ontario: https://www.ontario.ca/page/renting-ontario
